title.narrative: More and Better Jobs for Young Men and Women

description.narrative:
Rwanda faces significant challenges in creating decent and productive jobs for its youth, especially young women, who are disproportionately affected by unemployment. The "More and Better Jobs for Young Men and Women" initiative aims to address these challenges by promoting access to quality employment opportunities in Rwanda’s rapidly growing digital economy. In line with Rwanda's Vision 2050 and national development strategies, this project will focus on enhancing digital skills, promoting entrepreneurship, and improving job creation within the digital sector.
The project is designed to benefit young people aged 16 to 30, particularly those from secondary cities and Kigali, with a special emphasis on addressing the gender-specific barriers that young women face in accessing decent work. Through a combination of skills development, entrepreneurship support, and job placement initiatives, the project will create pathways for youth to transition into the digital economy, helping to reduce the current high rates of youth unemployment and underemployment.
The project, financially supported by the Government of Luxembourg, will be implemented over four years with a total budget of EUR 4 million. It will work closely with the Government of Rwanda, social partners, and the private sector to ensure that the skills and job opportunities created are aligned with market needs, thus fostering a more inclusive and resilient economy.
The expected outcomes of the project include increased access to digital jobs, improved digital skills among youth, and enhanced support for young entrepreneurs in the digital space. This initiative will contribute to Rwanda's broader development goals, including the promotion of inclusive economic growth, decent work, and gender equality, in line with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDG 8 on decent work and economic growth.
